questions.question: What is the base year for the Consumer Price Index series described in this note?
questions.explanation: The note states that the base year for the current series is 2012.
questions.source: The base year for the current series is 2012.

questions.question: According to the note, how many villages are covered by monthly price collection?
questions.explanation: Price data are collected from selected markets in 1181 villages, with 1114 urban markets covered separately.
questions.source: Price data are collected from selected markets in 1181 villages and 1114 urban markets every month.

questions.question: Which statement about the index formula is supported by the note?
options: It holds the basket fixed at base-year quantities
It re-weights the basket every month using current quantities
It averages base-year and current-year quantities
It chain-links the weights each quarter
questions.explanation: The note says a Laspeyres formula is used, which holds the basket fixed at base-year quantities.
questions.source: A Laspeyres formula is used, which holds the basket fixed at base-year quantities.

questions.question: Why can a fixed-basket index overstate the cost of living?
options: Because it does not capture consumers switching to cheaper alternatives
Because it excludes all services from the basket
Because it uses a geometric mean of price relatives
Because it is revised only once every ten years
questions.explanation: The note explains that the index can overstate the cost of living when consumers substitute towards cheaper alternatives.
questions.source: This means the index can overstate the cost of living when consumers substitute towards cheaper alternatives, a limitation known as substitution bias.

questions.question: The tendency of a fixed-basket index to overstate the cost of living is known as ______.
questions.explanation: The note names this limitation substitution bias.
questions.source: This means the index can overstate the cost of living when consumers substitute towards cheaper alternatives, a limitation known as substitution bias.

questions.question: For how long may the last reported price be carried forward when a market does not respond?
questions.explanation: Non-response is handled by carrying the last reported price forward for at most three months.
questions.source: Non-response in a selected market is handled by carrying forward the last reported price for a maximum of three months, after which the item is treated as temporarily unavailable.

questions.question: After what period of continuous unavailability is an item removed from the basket altogether?
questions.explanation: An item is dropped from the basket only after twelve consecutive months of unavailability.
questions.source: An item is dropped from the basket entirely only when it has been unavailable for twelve consecutive months.

questions.question: How does a point-to-point inflation rate differ from a month-on-month rate?
options: It compares a month with the same month a year earlier
It averages the preceding twelve months
It removes the effect of basket weights
questions.explanation: A point-to-point rate compares the index for a month with the same month of the previous year.
questions.source: A point-to-point inflation rate compares the index for a month with the index for the same month of the previous year.

questions.question: What size of change in a quotation triggers a validation query to the field office?
questions.explanation: A change larger than 25 per cent triggers a validation query before the quotation is accepted.
questions.source: A change larger than 25 per cent triggers a validation query to the field office before the quotation is accepted.

questions.question: An error must affect a published index by more than what amount before it is revised?
questions.explanation: Revisions are made only when an error affects the index by more than 0.1 index points.
questions.source: Revisions to a published index are made only when an error affects the index by more than 0.1 index points.

questions.question: A group shows the largest price rise this month but carries a very small weight. What should an analyst conclude about its effect on headline inflation?
options: Its contribution may still be small, so the weighted contribution should be read
It must be the largest contributor because its price rose most
Its weight should be increased before publication
Headline inflation should be recomputed without it
questions.explanation: The note warns that a group with a small weight can show a large price rise and still contribute little to headline inflation.
questions.source: A group with a small weight can show a large price rise and still contribute little to headline inflation.

questions.question: Where do the weights used in the basket come from?
questions.explanation: Weights are derived from the Consumer Expenditure Survey.
questions.source: Weights in the basket are derived from the Consumer Expenditure Survey and are revised when consumption patterns shift materially.

questions.question: How are seasonal items handled during months when they are out of season?
options: By dropping them from the index permanently
By repeating the previous year's price
questions.explanation: Seasonal items are handled by the class-mean imputation method when out of season.
questions.source: Seasonal items such as fresh fruit are handled by the class-mean imputation method during months when they are out of season.
